chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah

He explained them: in the Dhuhr prayer, twenty-one takbirations; in the Asr prayer, twenty-one takbirations; in the Maghrib prayer, sixteen takbirations; in the Isha' (last) prayer, twenty-one takbirations; in the Fajr prayer, eleven takbirations; and five takbirations of the Qunut in the five prayers.
ai.seo_question: How many takbirations are performed in each of the five daily prayers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific count of takbirations for each of the five daily prayers, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential tradition that distinguishes between the obligatory takbir of the opening (Takbirat al-Ihram) and those associated with Qunut. By detailing these counts, the hadith provides a precise liturgical framework for the physical structure of Salah, emphasizing the rhythmic glorification of God as an integral component of worship. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the Prophet’s and Imams’ specific methods of prayer as recorded in the major hadith collections.
